concepts.title: Accounting method
concepts.summary: Assign each operation a charge that may over- or under-pay its real cost. The analysis is valid exactly when stored credit never goes negative.

concepts.title: Amortised cost and the aggregate method
concepts.summary: Amortised cost is worst-case total over a sequence divided by the sequence length. No probability is involved, and the guarantee holds for every sequence.

concepts.title: Asymptotic running time analysis
concepts.summary: Fix the size measure and the case, count with summations or a recurrence, solve it, amortise where a sequence is involved, and state the tightest defensible bound.

concepts.title: Attention weights
concepts.summary: Attention weights are a softmax over scaled query-key dot products.

concepts.title: Average case needs a distribution
concepts.summary: Average-case time is an expectation over an assumed input distribution. A randomised algorithm instead averages over its own coins, so its bound holds for every input.

concepts.title: Big-O: the witness definition
concepts.summary: $f = O(g)$ when there exist constants $c > 0$ and $n_0$ with $f(n) \le c\,g(n)$ for all $n \ge n_0$. The bound need not be tight.

concepts.title: Big-Omega: the witness definition
concepts.summary: $f = \Omega(g)$ when there exist $c > 0$ and $n_0$ with $f(n) \ge c\,g(n)$ for all $n \ge n_0$: the same witness style, pointing the other way.

concepts.title: Comparing growth rates
concepts.summary: The limit of $f(n)/g(n)$ being $0$, a positive constant, or $\infty$ gives $o$, $\Theta$, or $\omega$, yielding the hierarchy $1 \prec \log\log n \prec \log n \prec n^{\epsilon} \prec n \prec n\log n \prec n^2 \prec 2^n \prec n!$.

concepts.title: Cost model and input size
concepts.summary: Running time is a function $T(n)$ counting primitive operations on a unit-cost RAM, where $n$ is a stated measure of input size.

concepts.title: Counting loops with summations
concepts.summary: A loop costs the sum of its body over its iterations, so nested loops become nested sums closed by arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic series identities.

concepts.title: Dot product
concepts.summary: The dot product of two vectors measures alignment, and is the sum of elementwise products.

concepts.title: Little-o and little-omega
concepts.summary: $f = o(g)$ quantifies over every $c > 0$, not merely some $c$, making it a strictly stronger separation than $O$. Little-omega is its mirror.

concepts.title: Log base is a constant factor
concepts.summary: Since $\log_a n = \log_b n / \log_b a$, every log base is $\Theta$ of every other and the base can be dropped. The base of an exponent cannot.

concepts.title: Master Theorem
concepts.summary: For $T(n) = a\,T(n/b) + f(n)$, compare $f(n)$ against $n^{\log_b a}$: the larger one wins, and a tie costs an extra $\log n$ factor.

concepts.title: Multi-head attention
concepts.summary: Several attention heads run in parallel over different learned subspaces, then concatenate.

concepts.title: Positional encoding
concepts.summary: Self-attention is permutation-equivariant, so order must be injected explicitly.

concepts.title: Potential method
concepts.summary: Set amortised cost to actual cost plus $\Phi(D_i) - \Phi(D_{i-1})$. If $\Phi(D_i) \ge \Phi(D_0)$ throughout, the telescoping sum bounds the true total.

concepts.title: Problem bounds vs algorithm bounds
concepts.summary: An upper bound exhibits one algorithm; a lower bound must quantify over all algorithms in a model, as the decision tree argument does for $\Omega(n\log n)$ comparison sorting.

concepts.title: Query key value projections
concepts.summary: Each token is projected into three roles: what it seeks, what it offers, and what it passes on.

concepts.title: ReAct loop
concepts.summary: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with tool calls, so each observation can revise the plan mid-flight.

concepts.title: Recursion tree method
concepts.summary: Expand the recurrence into a tree, sum each level, then sum the $\log_b n$ levels. The total is dominated by the root, the leaves, or spread evenly.

concepts.title: Self-attention
concepts.summary: Self-attention lets every token attend to every other token in the same sequence.

concepts.title: Softmax
concepts.summary: Softmax exponentiates a score vector and normalises it, producing a peaked probability distribution.

concepts.title: Substitution method
concepts.summary: Guess a closed form, then prove it by strong induction carrying the exact constants. Sometimes the hypothesis must be strengthened by subtracting a lower-order term.

concepts.title: Theta as both bounds
concepts.summary: $f = \Theta(g)$ exactly when $f = O(g)$ and $f = \Omega(g)$, so $f$ is sandwiched between $c_1 g$ and $c_2 g$ beyond some $n_0$. This is what tight means.

concepts.title: Tool calling
concepts.summary: A model emits a structured call against a declared schema; the harness executes it and returns the result into context.

concepts.title: Transformer block
concepts.summary: A transformer block is multi-head attention plus a feed-forward network, each wrapped in a residual connection and normalisation.

concepts.title: Vector as a list of numbers
concepts.summary: A vector is an element of a vector space; coordinates are a choice, not the object.

concepts.title: What asymptotics hides
concepts.summary: Dropping constants and low-order terms buys comparisons that survive a change of hardware, at the cost of hiding constants and crossover points that decide real runs.

concepts.title: Where the Master Theorem fails
concepts.summary: It is silent when $f$ and $n^{\log_b a}$ differ by less than a polynomial factor (e.g. $T(n)=2T(n/2)+n/\log n$), when regularity fails, and when subproblems differ in size.

concepts.title: Worst, best, average case
concepts.summary: The case picks which function of $n$ you are bounding; $O$, $\Omega$, $\Theta$ then bound it. They are independent axes, so O does not mean worst case.

concepts.title: Writing the recurrence
concepts.summary: Reading off the number of subcalls, each subproblem size, and the non-recursive work turns a recursive procedure into $T(n) = a\,T(n/b) + f(n)$ plus a base case.
